question: A diagnosis of cancer can be established on clinical and imaging grounds alone in cases of an obvious large breast mass with axillary lymphadenopathy, and chemotherapy may be started without histological confirmation.

l10n.wrongAnswerMessage: This statement is false. No matter how obvious a cancer appears clinically or radiologically, a tissue diagnosis is mandatory before starting treatment. The biopsy determines histological type, grade, receptor status (e.g., ER/PR/HER2 in breast cancer), and guides the treatment regimen.
l10n.correctAnswerMessage: Correct — this statement is FALSE. Tissue diagnosis (histology or cytology) is MANDATORY before initiating any cancer treatment, without exception. Clinically or radiologically 'obvious' cancers may turn out to be other pathologies (lymphoma vs carcinoma changes the regimen entirely), and molecular markers from biopsy are essential for treatment planning.
